messages:
nisha: quick RFC follow-up 1: i want to prototype decoupling ordering from the core batcher. idea: a pluggable OrderingPolicy interface so we can try score-based or affinity-preserving strategies. want feedback on safety, observability, and canary plan.

aj: primary objective? tail p99, fairness, or preserving kvcache affinity? can policies be hot-swapped without draining?

nisha: main goals = reduce tail latency and priority inversion for mixed workloads while keeping kvcache affinity for hot tenants. hot-swap via feature flags is desirable but start with shadow-mode + percent rollout.

oliver: head-of-line blocking + priority inversion worry me. reordering adds a reorder buffer and nondeterminism; must not violate per-GPU enqueue invariants. how do we bound worst-case latency?

sam: implementation thought: keep FIFO as default fast path. add a scoring hook applyScore(req) -> float; only reorder when score delta > threshold. collect pre/post histograms to measure impact.

maria: telemetry: p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies, token throughput, per-tenant kvcache_hit_rate, reorder_count, batches_affected, and kvcache_evictions_by_policy. tag metrics with policy_id.

chloe: migration: (1) shadow_ordering that records decisions + simulated batches for 100% traffic, (2) expose ordered_percent rollout flag to actually apply on a sample, (3) region canary. watch for race between admission and policy decisions.

devx: no SDK changes initially. keep behavior internal behind runtime flag. devx: we should document for SRE and customers what to expect if ordering increases request variance.

runtime-bot: ci/build: branch order-policy built, unit + integration (arrival trace sims) green :white_check_mark:

nisha: proposed experiment steps:
1) add OrderingPolicy interface: applyScore(request) -> float, optional tie-break key. default = FIFO.
2) add shadow mode recording (policy_id on each decision) and simulated batch composition.
3) add ordered_percent rollout (0/10/50/100). when >0 apply policy to selected requests.
4) collect metrics listed above and a reorder_rate gauge.
5) canary: us-west1 10% traffic x48h, expand if p999 within thresholds. immediate fallback to FIFO on error-budget trigger.

example config snippet: ```json {
  \"batcher\": {
    \"ordering\": {
      \"policy\": \"score_based_v1\",
      \"mode\": \"shadow\",
      \"ordered_percent\": 0,
      \"policy_id\": \"score_v1_2026-03\"
    }
  }
} ```

aj: i'll own telemetry dashboards (p99 delta by tenant, reorder_rate). will add alarm if p999 increases >10% vs baseline.

oliver: define eviction interplay: if policy moves a request away from a batch that would've hit kvcache, annotate potential cache_delta and prefer affinity when delta > epsilon. deterministic fallback: if per-GPU ordering can't be guaranteed, fallback to FIFO for that GPU.

sam: agree on deterministic fallback. recommend running the simulation harness over recent production traces to validate worst-case scenarios before canary.

nisha: next steps: spike impl + shadow-mode PR, run sims, add telemetry, 30m sync tomorrow to lock rollout thresholds. thanks.

sam: booked a 30m sync, will add agenda (metrics, rollback criteria, sim results). :thumbsup:
